name: Isometric Motion Graphics
visualIdentity: A supplemental direction: flat graphics or shallow 3D assembled on consistent isometric axes, with shared scale and lighting, visible top and side faces, contact shadows, modest thickness and 2D labels. Keep orthographic projection; restrained parallax is optional.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to 3D dioramas, miniature sets, constrained isometric scenes and layered 2.5D artwork. Useful for systems, infrastructure, logistics, data pipelines and product overviews; these applications are inferred from the combinations. For interactive HTML, focus, hover, pointer or scroll can reveal relationships or chapters.
limitations: Perspective shrinkage, camera tilt, drifting contact, exposed incomplete layers, excessive depth or obscured labels weaken the style. Omit parallax when projection or legibility suffers. Exploded reveals require real separable components and an explanatory purpose. Chapter transitions need meaningful boundaries; do not obscure causal links or violate a continuous-shot or loop requirement.
palette: Optional new-artwork suggestion only: background #F3EFE6, foreground #2C424F, accents #63968D and #C58662 (four discrete colors; gradients disabled). Supplied, brand, reference and existing semantic colors take precedence and retain exact values and roles. Accents are decorative, not body-text backgrounds: foreground on either accent misses the normal-text contrast target. Check actual composited frames; lighting and reflections do not license extra base hues.
motionAndInteraction: Move and assemble along the isometric axes; keep any depth parallax bounded and spatially coherent. Video motion must derive deterministically from seekable composition time, including direct and reverse seeks. HTML may map pointer input to small layer offsets, or scroll to reversible chapter/story progress with readable endpoints and holds. Keep labels fixed in screen-space; reduced-motion and keyboard access apply to interactive work. Optional candidate patterns must fit actual scene elements.
audio: Unspecified as a fixed style rule. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied assets and explicit requirements. Audio is optional, should support comprehension and motion, and must remain intelligible and unclipped when used.
assetRequirements: Use shallow geometry or layered artwork with consistent axes, scale and light; provide contact shadows and 2D copy. True 3D models are optional. Parallax needs separable layers and crop margins; exploded reveals need genuine component layers and labels. Exact fonts, models, soundtrack and source assets are unspecified.
combinations: Pair with style-109 diagram lines for axis-aligned connectors and flow paths, or style-095 flat UI for interface demonstrations on isometric devices. Preserve 2D labels, projection and one light direction. Suggested combinations and their use cases are guidance, not requirements.
productionApproach: Style renderer owns geometry, materials, lighting and typography; motion engine owns transforms and trajectories, one owner per animated property. Three.js with an orthographic camera and GSAP are recommended, not mandatory; native SVG/Canvas may suffice. HyperFrames is the primary video assembly, timing, sync, validation and export pipeline; Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, with reason recorded. Keep rendering and motion style-specific and deterministic. Interactive HTML has no required pipeline specified.
